section_summary: This section contains a comprehensive voluntary report (dated August 11, 1938) prepared by American Vice Consul Beppo R. Johansen at Yokohama on the training of personnel for the Japanese merchant marine, covering legal foundations, government nautical colleges, prefectural schools, curricula, practical training on sailing ships and in shipyards, and industry opinions. Following the report are State Department transmittal memoranda distributing copies to the U.S. Coast Guard, the Bureau of Marine Inspection and Navigation, and the U.S. Maritime Commission, which were then preparing a plan for training American seamen. Commendatory evaluations from these agencies praising the report as excellent are forwarded back to the consulate in Yokohama alongside State Department instruction ratings, and the section concludes with a document file note regarding the shipping of American seamen at Kobe.

subfiles.about: A voluntary consular report detailing the educational system, legal framework, and practical training programs for deck and engineer officers in the Japanese merchant marine.
subfiles.from: Beppo R. Johansen, American Vice Consul, Yokohama, Japan
subfiles.summary: This comprehensive voluntary report surveys Japan's merchant marine training system, focusing primarily on Tokyo Nautical College, Kobe Nautical College, and prefectural merchant marine schools. It examines the legal framework under Imperial and ministerial ordinances, historical development since 1875, admission standards, curricula for deck and engine departments, and mandatory naval reserve training. It also details practical instruction aboard auxiliary sailing training ships and in shipyards, the limited facilities for ordinary seamen, and evaluations by commercial shipping companies.
subfiles.title: Training Personnel for the Japanese Merchant Marine

subfiles.from: Thomas M. Woodward, Vice Chairman, United States Maritime Commission
subfiles.summary: Praises Johansen's report as adequate in form and substance, noting its value for the Commission's upcoming training plan report to Congress.
subfiles.title: Letter from United States Maritime Commission to the Secretary of State

subfiles.about: A letter commending Johansen's report as excellent and particularly timely for the Coast Guard's establishment of the U.S. Maritime Service.

subfiles.summary: Commends Johansen's report as excellent and timely, as the Coast Guard is inaugurating the U.S. Maritime Service training system for American seamen.
